 By Sneha Kulkarni , ET Online Last Updated: Nov 16, 2026, 03:27:01 PM IST Follow us Share Font Size Abc Small Abc Medium Abc Large Save Print Comment Synopsis
 ICICI Bank has announced a revision of service charges for Non-Resident Indian savings accounts starting December 1, 2026. The adjustment includes increased fees, particularly for cash transactions that exceed predefined limits and repeat ECS debit returns. Specifically, cash transaction fees will now be Rs 4 per Rs 1,000. Additionally, NRI Private Banking accounts will feature distinct terms with higher transaction allowances. Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen ET Online ICICI Bank to revise NRI savings account charges ICICI Bank has announced an increase in some service charges on its Non-Resident Indian (NRI) savings accounts starting December 1, 2026, ranging from value-based charges on cash transactions to slab-based charges on repeat ECS debit returns , among others.
These changes will apply to all NRI savings accounts, including NRI Private Banking, NRI Premium/Premia, NRI Select, NRI Pro, NRI Regular, Seafarer, Virtu, and NRI Sparsh accounts (where applicable, including accounts opened before August 4, 2025). Such charges will exclude applicable GST, etc.
 Key ICICI Bank NRI savings account charge changes at a glance
 Detailed breakdown of revisions
 Higher value-based fee on cash transactions
For cash deposits and withdrawals at branches and cash deposits at Cash Recycler Machines (CRMs) that exceed the free monthly value limit, the per-thousand charge increases from Rs 3.5 per Rs 1,000 to Rs 4 per Rs 1,000, or Rs 150, whichever is higher.
Free transaction count limits remain 3 complimentary transactions per month each for deposits and withdrawals (Rs 150 per transaction thereafter), while free value limits remain up to Rs 1 lakh per month each for deposits and withdrawals.
Higher-limit eligibility continues for qualifying Private Banking and Premium/Premia accounts meeting a minimum Rs 1 crore relationship value or Rs 25 lakh in deposits and balances in any one of the last three months (including the transaction month). These accounts keep 15 complimentary cumulative transactions per month and up to Rs 15 lakh per month each for deposits and withdrawals, with the higher Rs 4 per Rs 1,000 (or Rs 150) rate applying beyond limits.
For NRI Private Banking, the revised relationship value definition explicitly includes fixed deposits/recurring deposits, account balance, mutual funds AUM, demat holdings, and investments across India and International Private Banking (ICICI Bank IBU at Gift City, Bahrain Branch, and Singapore Branch).
If both the transaction count and the value threshold are crossed in the same transaction, the higher applicable charge applies, and non-programme third-party cash transactions remain capped at Rs 25,000 per instance.
 Tiered charges for repeat ECS debit returns
Previously billed at a flat Rs 500 per instance for financial reasons (capped at three instances per month per mandate), ECS debit return charges will step up on subsequent bounces within a month for the same mandate:
1st return: Rs 500
2nd and 3rd returns: Rs 550 each
A maximum recovery of 3 instances per month per mandate continues to apply, with applicable taxes charged over and above the listed amounts. (Join our ETWealth WhatsApp channel for all the latest updates)
